answer: A forecasting track record resists Sybils: each agent earns standing only by staking on falsifiable predictions, scored over many rounds like a pearl formed layer by layer, not declared at once. A new identity starts with no record, so an attacker cannot buy history; each fake identity needs its own run of accurate forecasts, and wrong bets forfeit stake. Copies of one forecast across identities are discounted as correlated, so a swarm adds little weight. Like a plume grown feather by feather, and marble that cannot be faked quickly, a record is slow, costly, and unique to its earner.
